text:
Maya (CS): Quick heads-up — prepping Hummingbird QBR. Onboarding has an embedding-heavy run and we saw a sharp token spike last week. Renewal in ~30d. Need a short (1-slide) burn + mitigation list by Fri. Who can own the forecast?

Simon (FinOps): Pulling raws now. Quick snapshot: last 7d tokens = 4,800,312; extrapolated monthly = ~20M tokens. Using current tiering that maps to ~$12k/mo. Sending a tiny CSV below.

Simon (FinOps): ```date,tokens,cost
2024-04-01,420000,2400
2024-04-02,510000,2900
2024-04-03,680000,3900
2024-04-04,770000,4300
2024-04-05,1200000,6600```

budget-bot: ALERT: Hummingbird daily threshold breached on 2024-04-05 (1.2M tokens). Reason tag: embed-batch. Suggested immediate actions: throttle job concurrency OR apply temporary credits. :warning:

Leo (AM): Is that mostly an initial indexing run or continuous usage? Customer said they’d batch-import ~30M rows. If it's one-time we can offer a short-term credits package and show impact.

Ana (Solutions): Checked their pipeline — 95% of tokens are from the embedding stage (embed model: open-embed-large-quant). They run 8 parallel workers, no prefix caching enabled. Ops suggestions: reduce parallelism to 2, enable prefix/KV caching, and add per-job rate-limit. Also schedule the remaining heavy imports to midnight PT for lower SLO pressure.

Maya (CS): Nice. For QBR we need: 1) burn chart (Simon) 2) mitigation playbook (Ana) 3) renewal ask + optional reserved commit proposal (Leo). I'll draft the slide deck. Can someone run a 30/60/90-day forecast with and without mitigations?

Simon (FinOps): Running a quick forecast query now:
```sql
SELECT day, SUM(tokens) as tokens
FROM usage
WHERE account = 'hummingbird' AND day >= '2024-04-01'
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day;
```
Result (w/o mitigations): est monthly tokens = 19.8M; with Ana's mitigations (est 55% drop in batch tokens) -> ~9M tokens/month.

budget-bot: Forecast job queued by @Simon. ETA ~3m. Preliminary: projected monthly tokens = 19.8M, projected cost = $11,880. With suggested ops changes projected tokens = 8.9M, projected cost = $5,340. Renewal risk flag: medium if runway < 45d.

Maya (CS): Awesome. Leo — can you propose a 3-month reserved commit that shows unit economics improvement? Customer cares about predictable costs. If they commit 60% of current avg, we should give a tiered discount and put a guardrail for burst.

Leo (AM): Will draft options. Quick ask: do we have a one-page 'temporary credits + throttle' offer we can send to reduce immediate friction?

Ana (Solutions): I'll assemble the ops playbook snippet and a one-click runbook:
- Reduce workers to 2
- Turn on prefix caching
- Limit batch-size to 5k rows
- Run large imports between 00:00-06:00 PT
- Apply 10% credits from startup pool
I'll paste the playbook as a Gist and the steps for them to toggle in Console.

Maya (CS): Action items: Simon — finalize forecast + burn chart (EOD). Ana — playbook + Gist (EOD). Leo — commit options + one-pager for credits (Tues). I'll schedule customer QBR tentatively Tue 10:00 PT and start the slide. Tagging @Simon and @Ana. :calendar:

budget-bot: Forecast complete. Monthly baseline tokens: 19,824,312; monthly baseline cost: $11,894. Next steps: create renewal runbook if commit < 60% and runway < 45d.

Simon (FinOps): Uploaded burn graph to the QBR drive: https://drive.example/reports/hummingbird/burn-2024-04.png

Maya (CS): Thanks all — will draft the email to the customer with MITIGATION plan + meeting invite. If we still see >1M/day tomorrow, we'll escalate to credits pool. :+1:

Leo (AM): I'll prep the pricing scenario slides.

Ana (Solutions): Gist with toggles: https://gist.github.com/anadev/hummingbird-ops-playbook. Putting the exact Console toggle steps there.

Maya (CS): Closing loop: anyone else to add? If not, I'll mark this thread for the QBR packet. :eyes:
